meta.mechanism: PCSK9 inhibitor (fully human monoclonal antibody); increases hepatic LDL receptor recycling
meta.modality: monoclonal antibody (subcutaneous 75 mg Q2W, blinded titration to 150 mg Q2W; blinded switch to placebo if LDL-C <15 mg/dL twice)
meta.indication: secondary prevention after recent acute coronary syndrome (1-12 months) on high-intensity or maximum-tolerated statin

n_randomized.quote: Patients were randomly assigned to receive alirocumab subcutaneously at a dose of 75 mg (9462 patients) or matching placebo (9462 patients) every 2 weeks.
n_randomized.note: Total 18,924 ('a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 18,924 patients'). Registry S4 enrollment 18924 ACTUAL.

median_followup.quote: The median duration of follow-up was 2.8 years.
median_followup.note: Slides S3: 'median 2.8 (Q1–Q3 2.3–3.4) years'. FDA label S8: 'The median follow-up duration was 33 months.'

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal or nonfatal ischemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalization
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary end point was a composite of death from coronary heart disease, nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal or nonfatal ischemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalization.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: ACS 1-12 months earlier; on atorvastatin 40-80 / rosuvastatin 20-40 mg or max tolerated dose; LDL-C >=70 mg/dL OR non-HDL-C >=100 mg/dL OR apoB >=80 mg/dL; age >=40
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: 18,924 patients who had an acute coronary syndrome 1 to 12 months earlier, had a low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol level of at least 70 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter), a non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol level of at least 100 mg per deciliter (2.6 mmol per liter), or an apolipoprotein B level of at least 80 mg per deciliter, and were receiving statin therapy at a high-intensity dose or at the maximum tolerated dose.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Age >=40 from registry S4 exclusion criteria ('Age < 40 years').

planned_events.quote: Based on the above assumptions, 1613 events are needed for 90% power.
planned_events.location: Statistical Analysis Plan v3 (11-Oct-2017), sample size section
planned_events.note: Also in design paper S6 abstract (pub 2014-08-07): 'The trial is expected to continue until 1613 primary end point events have occurred with minimum follow-up of at least 2 years, providing 90% power to detect a 15% hazard reduction.' Observed: 1955 primary events (903+1052).

assumed_rrr.quote: Treatment hazard ratio of 0.85 (corresponding to a 15% hazard risk reduction for the test group relative to placebo), which is assumed to be constant over time;
assumed_rrr.location: Statistical Analysis Plan, sample size assumptions
assumed_rrr.note: Design rationale (S15, open PMC): 'Design assumptions were a primary end point incidence of 11.4% at 4 years in the placebo group and a median baseline LDL-C level of 90 mg/dL (2.33 mmol/L), reduced by 50% with alirocumab treatment, resulting in an expected 15% hazard reduction.' I.e. ~45 mg/dL (~1.16 mmol/L) assumed LDL-C difference.

power.quote: A log-rank test at an overall 1-sided 2.5% significance level with 90% power;
power.location: Statistical Analysis Plan, sample size assumptions

alpha.quote: A log-rank test at an overall 1-sided 2.5% significance level with 90% power;
alpha.location: Statistical Analysis Plan, sample size assumptions
alpha.note: Equivalent to two-sided 0.05. Two interim analyses with Gamma(-22) alpha-spending; SAP final-analysis boundary mentions '0.0249 1-sided alpha level'.

stopped_early.quote: Final analysis date: when 1613 patients have experienced at least 1 primary efficacy event
stopped_early.note: Not stopped early; interim analyses at ~50% and ~75% of events (design paper S6) did not stop the trial. Trial ran to completion (registry primary completion 2018-01-23).

baseline.quote: The mean LDL-C value at baseline was 92.4 mg/dL.
baseline.note: ~2.39 mmol/L. FDA prescribing information, current version (effective 2026-07-07). NEJM main-text baseline value not accessed (abstract only). The design assumed a median baseline LDL-C of 90 mg/dL (S15).

baseline.quote: Baseline lipoprotein(a) levels (median: 21.2 mg/dl; interquartile range [IQR]: 6.7 to 59.6 mg/dl)
baseline.note: Bittner et al. JACC 2020, prespecified analysis; abstract only.
NOT FOUND (NEJM Table 1 / supplement not accessed).

biomarker_effects.method: calculated (Friedewald) LDL-C; measured LDL-C used when both available (SAP S5)
biomarker_effects.quote: Percent Change From Baseline in Calculated LDL-C at Months 4, 12, and 48: ITT Analysis ... Month 4: Placebo 4.4 (SE 0.3); Alirocumab -55.8 (SE 0.3)
biomarker_effects.location: Registry results, other pre-specified outcome measure
biomarker_effects.note: Quote assembled from registry structured result fields (title + arm values). change_pct = -55.8 - (+4.4) = -60.2 percentage points (derived from registry LS means). change_abs derived from company slides S3 mean ITT LDL-C at month 4: alirocumab 39.8 vs placebo 93.3 mg/dL -> -53.5 mg/dL = -1.38 mmol/L. CTT check (derived): 0.78^1.38 = 0.71 expected RR over ~5 y vs observed HR 0.85 at median 2.8 y. SAP: 'Calculated LDL-C is obtained using the Friedewald formula.'

biomarker_effects.location: Registry results, ITT LDL-C percent change
biomarker_effects.note: Quote assembled from registry structured fields. Derived difference -53.7 pp. Absolute from slides S3: 48.0 vs 96.4 mg/dL -> -48.4 mg/dL = -1.25 mmol/L.

biomarker_effects.location: Registry results, ITT LDL-C percent change
biomarker_effects.note: Quote assembled from registry structured fields. Derived difference -39.9 pp. Absolute from slides S3: 66.4 vs 103.1 mg/dL -> -36.7 mg/dL = -0.95 mmol/L. ITT attenuation reflects treatment discontinuation (14.2%) and blinded switch to placebo (7.7%); on-treatment alirocumab LDL-C was 37.6/42.3/53.3 mg/dL at months 4/12/48 (slides S3).

biomarker_effects.unit: mg/dL (absolute, ITT means at month 4, from slide)
biomarker_effects.quote: LDL-C: ITT and On-Treatment Analyses ... Placebo ITT 93.3 ... Alirocumab ITT 39.8
biomarker_effects.note: Values read from labeled data points in figure (rendered slide image); -1.38 mmol/L (derived using 38.67 mg/dL per mmol/L).

biomarker_effects.quote: Alirocumab reduced lipoprotein(a) by 5.0 mg/dl (IQR: 0 to 13.5 mg/dl), corrected LDL-C by 51.1 mg/dl (IQR: 33.7 to 67.2 mg/dl), and reduced the risk of MACE
biomarker_effects.note: Abstract does not state whether placebo-adjusted or the exact timepoint (Lp(a) measured at randomization, 4 and 12 months). Percent change NOT FOUND. Corrected LDL-C (for Lp(a)-cholesterol) reduction 51.1 mg/dL.
NOT FOUND: ODYSSEY OUTCOMES apoB change not located in accessible sources (NEJM full text/supplement not accessed).

biomarker_effects.quote: SAR236553 demonstrated a clear dose-response relationship with respect to percentage LDL-C lowering for both Q2W and Q4W administration: 40%, 64%, and 72% with 50, 100, and 150 mg Q2W, respectively, and 43% and 48% with 200 and 300 mg Q4W. LDL-C reduction with placebo at week 12 was 5%.
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2 on atorvastatin, n=183, published 2012-03-28 (pre-readout). Values are within-arm % change; placebo -5%, so placebo-adjusted ~ -67% (derived). Abstract also notes reductions in non-HDL-C, apoB and Lp(a) without numbers.

biomarker_effects.timepoint: week 24 (phase 3 ODYSSEY LONG TERM, 150 mg Q2W)
biomarker_effects.quote: At week 24, the difference between the alirocumab and placebo groups in the mean percentage change from baseline in calculated LDL cholesterol level was -62 percentage points (P<0.001); the treatment effect remained consistent over a period of 78 weeks.
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 3 lipid trial (n=2341), published 2015-03-15 (pre-readout). Post hoc MACE 1.7% vs 3.3%, HR 0.52 (0.31-0.90). FDA label S8 Table 3 gives -58% LDL-C, -50% non-HDL-C, -51% apoB at week 24 for the same trial (different imputation model).

biomarker_effects.location: FDA label Table 3 (columns LDL-C, Total-C, Non-HDL-C, Apo B)
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout phase 3 lipid evidence; label version read is current (2026), table describes 2015 trial. non-HDL-C -50%.

hr.quote: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 0.93; P<0.001).
hr.note: Registry S4 and press release S2 identical. All-cause death HR 0.85 (0.73-0.98), nominal; CHD death HR 0.92 (0.76-1.11).

p.note: Quote assembled from registry structured analysis fields. NEJM abstract S1: 'P<0.001'; press release S2: 'p=0.0003'.

events_treatment.quote: A composite primary end-point event occurred in 903 patients (9.5%) in the alirocumab group

events_control.quote: and in 1052 patients (11.1%) in the placebo group

safety_signals.value: Local injection-site reactions more frequent: 3.8% vs 2.1%
safety_signals.quote: The incidence of adverse events was similar in the two groups, with the exception of local injection-site reactions (3.8% in the alirocumab group vs. 2.1% in the placebo group).

safety_signals.value: No excess neurocognitive events (1.5% vs 1.8%) or new-onset diabetes (9.6% vs 10.1%)
safety_signals.quote: There was no difference in neurocognitive events (1.5% Praluent; 1.8% placebo) or new-onset diabetes (9.6% Praluent; 10.1% placebo).

safety_signals.value: 730 patients (7.7%) switched to placebo in a blinded fashion after two consecutive LDL-C <15 mg/dL
safety_signals.quote: Overall, 730 (7.7%) of 9,451 patients switched to placebo.
safety_signals.note: Design feature limiting very low LDL-C exposure; dilutes ITT LDL-C difference.

genetics.finding: PCSK9 nonsense (loss-of-function) mutations associated with 28% lower LDL-C and 88% lower CHD risk (black ARIC participants); R46L 15% lower LDL-C, 47% lower CHD (whites)
genetics.quote: Of the 3363 black subjects examined, 2.6 percent had nonsense mutations in PCSK9; these mutations were associated with a 28 percent reduction in mean LDL cholesterol and an 88 percent reduction in the risk of CHD

genetics.finding: PCSK9 and HMGCR variants give near-identical CV protection per unit LDL-C
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level

genetics.finding: CTT: RR 0.78 per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction for major vascular events (calculator benchmark)
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

consensus_explanation.summary: Genetically validated target (PCSK9 LoF) with a large placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction (~54 mg/dL, ~1.4 mmol/L at month 4, ITT). Same-class proof from FOURIER was already public a year before readout. The trial enrolled a very high-risk post-ACS population on high-intensity statins and was powered for a realistic 15% RRR (1613 events, 90% power). The observed HR of 0.85 matched the design assumption exactly. Relative benefit was smaller than a 5-year CTT extrapolation because of short follow-up (median 2.8 y), ITT dilution of the LDL-C difference over time (discontinuation, blinded switch to placebo at LDL-C <15 mg/dL) and modest baseline LDL-C (~92 mg/dL). Benefit was greatest when baseline LDL-C was >=100 mg/dL (MACE HR 0.76). Safety clean apart from injection-site reactions.

Placebo-adjusted LDL-C % change is derived from registry LS-mean within-arm % changes (ITT); the NEJM article may report differences computed differently (on-treatment vs ITT).
Absolute LDL-C differences derived from figure labels on company slides (mean ITT LDL-C), not a reported between-group difference with CI.
Lp(a) 5.0 mg/dL median reduction (Bittner, abstract only): placebo adjustment and timepoint unclear; percent reduction NOT FOUND.

CTT comparison caveat (derived): expected RR 0.78^1.38 = 0.71 using month-4 ITT difference, or ~0.78^1.2 = 0.74 using a rough time-averaged difference, vs observed 0.85 at median 2.8 y; the ITT LDL-C difference shrank to 0.95 mmol/L by month 48.
